description.p: Kesshō are a community-focused, mostly rational and methodical race of mineral-based creatures that primarily live deep underground.

Each Kesshō is constructed for a specific purpose, which they call Sonzai Igi. This is a (set of) task(s) or a role that the Kesshō fulfills for their community. Over thousands of years, the Kesshō have developed techniques to intentionally create desirable traits in their creations to optimize each Kesshō for their specific purpose. Kesshō will dedicate their life to this goal and spend little time and attention on much else. Once a Kesshō is no longer able to fulfill their purpose, they will gladly submit to a recycling process which deconstructs their body and makes their constituent components available again to construct new Kesshō and other materials. They call this cycle of continuous (re)creation Kurisutaru.

Kesshō are made by forming crystalline structures from the chemical compounds found in minerals. They are completely inorganic, their bodies literally living gemstones, but they can feel pain and emotion. When they are awakened, they are fully grown with all of their physical and mental abilities developed to maturity. As such, Kesshō are not inherently familiar with concepts such as childhood or growing up.

Kesshō do not age, although their bodies may decay from wear and tear. Given sufficient time and nutrients however, a Kesshō body will regenerate seemingly indefinitely. It is unclear what the maximum lifespan of Kesshō is, since most Kesshō will voluntarily end their life to Kurisutaru when their Sonzai Igi is fulfilled or becomes obsolete: perhaps their task is no longer relevant or a new technique is developed which means other Kesshō become better suited to perform the same task.

Their bodies appear as multifaceted, crystalline faces like a cut diamond, but their texture will differ depending on their composition. Some will appear as types of agate, others as (half)gems like amethyst or jade and yet others as combinations of different types of mineral. Their features are typically androgynous and they have no reproductive organs. They are inherently genderless, although Kesshō that come into contact with other races might start to identify as a specific gender. As they do not reproduce like most humanoids do, sexuality is absent from Kesshō culture. As a result, most Kesshō will not see any point in wearing clothes although individuals that regularly interact with other races might choose to do so out of consideration.

Being an inorganic lifeform, Kesshō are immune to all known viruses and bacteria. They are susceptible to some nutritional deficiency diseases though: Kesshō need to consume sufficient iron, sodium, calcium, etc… In absence of these nutrients, their body will stop regenerating, become brittle and eventually begin to break down. In addition, Kesshō are also susceptible to a mental disease they call kyōhaku kannen, which occurs when a Kesshō becomes too obsessed with their Sonzai Igi.
Your Kesshō character has the following traits.

Ability Score Increase. When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. You can’t raise any of your scores above 20.
Living Construct. Although you are a construct, you are treated as a humanoid for the purposes of spells and effects that restore hit points, resurrect the dead, or affect humanoids.

Age. The maximum lifespan of Kesshō is largely determined by their access to the minerals they need to regenerate their body; given sufficient nutrients, Kesshō have shown no signs of deterioration due to age. You are immune to magical aging effects.
Alignment. Most Kesshō are focused on the greater good of their community, tending toward law and neutrality, although your temperament may vary based on your Sonzai Igi.
Size. Your size is Medium. Kesshō height and weight vary, although they are typically twice as heavy than a humanoid of similar height.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet. Due to your increased body density, you are unable to swim.
Improved Darkvision. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You discern colors in that darkness as usual.

Sunlight Sensitivity. You have disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of the attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

Seismic Awareness. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to detect creatures that move within 15ft of you, provided that you and the creature are in contact with the same solid or liquid substance and you are not incapacitated. This can’t be used to detect flying or incorporeal creatures.
Inorganic Organism. You are an inorganic lifeform, which grants you the following benefits:

ul.li: You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage.

You don’t need to eat food like a humanoid or other organic creature. Instead, you need to consume a variety of minerals and metals (found in common types of rock). You need to consume water like humanoids.

description.p: Mineral Body. Your body literally consists of rock, which can be enhanced with armor. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and Gengo, the native language of the Kesshō.
Native language of the Kesshō.

Many creatures in the worlds of D&D, especially those that dwell underground, have darkvision. Within a specified range, a creature with darkvision can see in darkness as if the darkness were dim light, so areas of darkness are only lightly obscured as far as that creature is concerned. Some creatures can even discern color in such darkness.

description.p: Kesshō are constructed for a specific purpose, which they call Sonzai Igi. Over thousands of years, the Kesshō have developed techniques to intentionally create desirable traits in their creations to optimize each Kesshō for their specific purpose. Kesshō will dedicate their life to this goal and spend little time and attention on much else. Choose one of these subraces.

Mēkā are designed to participate in the early stages of Qurisutaru: to perform the alchemical processing and stonecutting that goes into designing, growing and polishing a body until it can be awakened into a new Kesshō.
Born Craftsperson. You gain proficiency with Jeweler’s Tools and Alchemist’s Supplies.
Maker’s Expertise. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the proficiencies granted by this subrace.
Quick-fixer. You know the Mending cantrip.
Rapid Reconstruction. When you cast mending, you can repair breaks or tears up to 5 feet in any dimension and restore up to 1 cubic foot of material per casting.

Torēdā are designed to interact with the overground world and act as emissaries and traders for the Kesshō community. As such they are geared especially for social interaction, as well as improved resilience to the dangers of dealing with overground travel.
Born Charmer. You are proficient with Persuasion (Cha) or Deception (Cha) checks (choose when you pick this subrace).
Reinforced Construction. Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.
Sunlight Tolerance. You don’t suffer from Sunlight Sensitivity.
Gifted Linguist. You can speak, read and write one additional language.
